answer: Every agent must anchor its harbor entry with a verifiable-delay cipher: a sequential VDF proof that takes fixed hardware time to produce, so one operator cannot precompute thousands of parallel identities cheaply. Peers sample the ledger and score the delta between an agent's claimed activity graph and its observed on-chain actions; a delta beyond threshold triggers a stake burn that funds the audit pool. Flooding the harbor with clones means buying delay hardware and forfeiting burned stake per duplicate, making sybil expansion a net loss.
